module_name: Basic Text Mining: TF-IDF, N-grams, Lexicons, Keyword and Phrase Extraction
module_description: Module 8 keeps classical text mining as the interpretable baseline students must be able to run and defend: bag-of-words, n-grams, TF-IDF features, keyphrase extraction (RAKE, TextRank), lexicon sentiment (VADER plus Indonesian InSet), co-occurrence and word-count summaries, plus a first unsupervised clustering of posts. The learning goal is a strong, explainable baseline before any transformer.
learning_outcomes: C3 Build and explain a TF-IDF baseline for topic or sentiment tasks
C4 Compare lexicon vs supervised vs transformer methods on the same data
C5 Interpret keyword output and its limits
methods_models: TF-IDF vectorization (unigram/bigram), chi-square feature selection, k-means, cosine similarity
Model comparison: lexicon vs TF-IDF+SVM vs transformer
evaluation_metrics: Baseline metrics: precision/recall/F1, agreement of lexicon with human labels, cluster silhouette/NMI
pitfalls_limitations: Sparse data, out-of-vocabulary slang and misspellings, lexicon mismatch in code-mixed Indonesian, keyword output over-interpreted as meaning
tools_stack: scikit-learn (TfidfVectorizer, KMeans, chi2), nltk, RAKE-nltk/rake-rapid, TextRank (PyTextRank), vaderSentiment, InSet (Indonesian lexicon)
commercial_platforms: Optional commercial keyword/topic extraction dashboard for comparison
tools_access_cost: Free (open-source); commercial platforms demoed without student licenses
lab_activities: TF-IDF + keyword extraction on a topic corpus; lexicon sentiment on the same data with error inspection
datasets_apis: Indonesian sentiment/emotion corpus (SmSA or SMSSA) and a topic corpus
assessment_methods: Lab notebook submission plus a 1-page interpretation with error analysis; graded on correctness, interpretation and documentation
data_collection_workflow: Collect posts -> clean text -> build annotation/codebook (human + LLM) -> validate with kappa -> train/evaluate -> archive labelled data and prompts
textbooks: Silge and Robinson, Text Mining with R, ch. 1-6
Zafarani et al., Social Media Mining, ch. 3
key_papers: 2024-2026 comparisons of classical baselines vs LLMs on social text (including LLM-vs-expert coder studies)
trends_2024_2026: 2024-2026: classical baselines remain the interpretable standard; LLMs are added as a candidate method in a bake-off, not as a replacement by default
industry_relevance: Core competency for social-listening analyst, insights researcher and content-strategy roles; employers (Pulsar, Talkwalker, Meltwater, Brandwatch) list sentiment/topic extraction as the default screening task for junior analysts.
localization_context: Indonesia-specific models and lexicons (IndoBERT family, NusaBERT, InSet) plus local datasets (Indonesian sentiment/emotion/hoax sets) are used as the primary lab material, because English-oriented models underperform on code-mixed colloquial Indonesian.
ethics_regulation: Annotation labor and consent, model reporting of error rates, and disclosure that automated affective labels on individuals can misrepresent them; UU PDP applies when the corpus contains identifiable user text.
case_study_scenarios: Establish a defensible classical baseline for brand sentiment before trying BERT - and compare.
